venue.name: The Port Theatre
venue.description: The Port Theatre is an 804 seat performing arts centre on Nanaimo's waterfront, co-managed by the Port Theatre Society and the City of Nanaimo. It runs over 250 events a year, most of them booked by touring promoters and community groups renting the hall. The Society's own Spotlight Series includes family shows and, in its own words, school shows for young audiences. No school show is listed for the current season, and there is no education or teachers section on the site.

facility_notes.washrooms: We offer accessible single-occupancy gender-neutral washroom options on all levels of the facility. When entering the lobby, washrooms are located on the right-hand side of the building on the first and second floors.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: One elevator, over 28 wheelchair and accessible seating options, complimentary in-house wheelchairs and hearing assistance devices. Many seats require some stairs, so the theatre asks you to call the Ticket Centre before buying.

restrictions: Your child will need a ticket and their own seat
Infants under the age of 24 months may sit on the lap of an accompanying adult during family events and certain community performances
The Port Theatre strives to be a scent-free environment
We only allow bottled water in the auditorium
There are no refunds or ticket exchanges. All sales are final
venue.hours_notes: Ticket Centre: Monday to Friday 11am to 5pm, Saturday 12pm to 5pm, and 2 hours before ticketed showtimes. Closed Saturdays in July and August. Administration office: Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: The presented season runs from fall to spring. The 2026 to 2027 Spotlight Series runs from October 2026 to May 2027, with six Coffee Concerts on Tuesday mornings at 10:30am.

programs.name: School show
programs.description: The Port Theatre Society says its Spotlight Series includes school shows for young audiences, and the events listing carries a School Shows series you can filter by. As of the start of September 2026 that filter returns no events and the school shows section of the season page is empty. Nothing is published about price, ages, dates, group size or how a class books.
programs.our_note: Nothing is scheduled and nothing is published, so this is a phone call rather than a booking. Ask the Ticket Centre whether a school show is coming this season and what a class pays. The student prices you can see on the site are for the public evening shows, not for a class booking.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms on every floor, an elevator and over 28 accessible seats. Parking is paid city street parking, and bus parking, drop off and lunch space are not covered anywhere on the site.
programs.evidence: These include evening performances inside the theatre, morning coffee concerts, and school shows for young audiences.

programs.name: Family performance tickets
programs.description: The Port Theatre Society programmes family shows inside its own Spotlight Series and sells single tickets for them. For the family clown show Glob on 23 November 2026, which the site marks All Ages and 65 minutes with no intermission, tickets are $35 regular and $25 student, with taxes and fees included. It starts at 6:00pm. Prices are set show by show, so check the event page for the one you want. Every child needs their own ticket and their own seat.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the auditorium and watch, for about an hour with no interval. An usher can bring a free booster seat so a smaller child can see over the row in front.
programs.our_note: The $25 is their student price rather than a children's price, and no group or class rate is published, so ask the Ticket Centre what a block of seats for a class costs. Most shows start at 7:30pm, so check the time before you plan around a school day. Tickets are final sale with no refunds or exchanges.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms on every level, an elevator, over 28 accessible seats, and a free coat check and booster seats at the services desk. Parking is paid street parking handled by the city, and bus parking and lunch space are not mentioned.
programs.extra_fees_note: Members save $5 on each regular Spotlight ticket. Ticket prices include all taxes and fees.
programs.cancellation_note: There are no refunds or ticket exchanges. All sales are final.

gaps: There is no education, teachers or school programs page anywhere on the site.

The School Shows series exists in their events filter but returns no events, and the school shows section of the season page is an empty heading. This was checked in a browser as well as by fetch, so it is genuinely empty rather than a rendering problem.

No group rate and no class rate is published. The only reduced prices on the site are a student ticket price on individual shows and a Discovery Series student price of $13.50, and neither is described as a school or group rate.
The Discovery Series page still says the 2025 to 2026 shows have yet to be announced, so that page has not been updated for the current season.
No lead time, no group size limit and no booking route is published for a school or class booking.
Nothing about lunch space, bus parking or where a bus can drop off. The site sends you to the City of Nanaimo for parking options and fees.
Whether an adult chaperone gets in free is not stated. Every person including each child needs their own ticket and seat.
The family concerts held here at $39.50 adult and $25 youth under 18 are presented by the Vancouver Island Symphony rather than by the Port Theatre, so those prices are the symphony's to confirm.
The site publishes no coordinates and no map with a marked point, so the location here comes from the street address.
There is no theatre school, no workshop and no education program on the site. The only youth activity mentioned is an audition call for the Nutcracker.
No photographs of the auditorium or lobby are published, so the pictures here are the outside of the building and one touring company's promotional shot.
The theatre gives out complimentary community tickets to Spotlight and Discovery events through partner organisations. No route to ask for them is published, but it is worth raising.
